grade.rationale: The route helpers are concise, readable, and mostly preserve sensible invariants. The main weakness is incomplete numeric validation when serializing a location index.

summary: The implementation is straightforward and generally correct. One low-severity edge case allows non-finite numbers to be written as invalid query-parameter values. Test coverage is unknown because no coverage evidence was supplied, and ESLint evidence was unavailable due to missing dependencies.

grade.rationale: Normal fingerprints and finite location indices are read and written correctly, with negative and fractional indices normalized appropriately.
The functions are small, cohesive, and use standard URLSearchParams operations without unnecessary abstraction.
Names and control flow clearly communicate the query-string representation and normalization behavior.
Reading rejects invalid integers, but writing does not guard against NaN or infinities before serialization.
Both helpers are deterministic and easy to exercise with table-driven unit tests; actual coverage remains unknown.

findings.title: Non-finite location indices are serialized into the route
findings.description: Math.max and Math.floor do not sanitize every JavaScript number: NaN becomes the literal query value "NaN", while positive Infinity becomes "Infinity". Although the reader later converts these values to index 0, the writer can still emit malformed, non-canonical route state, making its input invariant weaker than its number type suggests.
findings.recommendation: Validate locationIndex with Number.isFinite before flooring and clamping it, choosing a documented fallback such as 0 for non-finite values. Add unit cases for NaN, positive and negative Infinity, negative values, and fractional values.
